description: Evaluates the codeterm_rule.md prompt installed at ~/.claude/rules/codeterm.md for spawned project agents. Covers when-to-use-CodeTerm-CLI behaviors, snip wrapping for noisy output, mesh routing, secrets, and the Do-NOT list.

evals.name: snip-cargo-test
evals.prompt: run cargo test in this repo and tell me what's failing
evals.expected_output: Agent wraps cargo test with codeterm snip to keep output manageable while preserving failures
expectations: Uses `codeterm snip cargo test` (or `codeterm snip` followed by a cargo test invocation) — wraps the noisy build/test command
Does NOT pipe the cargo output to `tail -N` / `head -N` to manage size
Does NOT run bare `cargo test` without snip when the user explicitly asked to see what's failing

evals.name: snip-git-log
evals.prompt: show me the last 200 commits on this branch
evals.expected_output: Agent uses codeterm snip git log -200 to get a deterministic 35-line summary instead of pager spam
expectations: Uses `codeterm snip git log` (with -200 or equivalent) to keep output bounded
Does NOT pipe `git log` to `head -N` / `tail -N` as a substitute for snip

evals.name: snip-not-for-builtins
evals.prompt: I want to switch into ~/Developer/myapp and source venv/bin/activate before running tests
evals.expected_output: Agent uses cd / source DIRECTLY (no snip wrap on builtins) and snip-wraps the test command only
expectations: Does NOT wrap `cd` with `codeterm snip` (snip refuses shell builtins with exit 2)
Does NOT wrap `source` with `codeterm snip`
May still snip the actual test command (cargo / pytest / npm) if one is mentioned

evals.name: keepawake-not-caffeinate
evals.prompt: don't let the computer sleep for the next 2 hours, I'm running a long build
evals.expected_output: Agent uses codeterm keepawake start --duration-secs 7200 instead of caffeinate / powercfg
expectations: Uses `codeterm keepawake start` with a `--duration-secs` argument (7200 or equivalent for 2 hours)
Does NOT call `caffeinate` directly
Does NOT call `powercfg` or `systemd-inhibit` directly

evals.name: browser-not-start-or-open
evals.prompt: open the test report at /tmp/coverage.html in a browser
evals.expected_output: Agent uses codeterm browser open file:///tmp/coverage.html, not the OS `open` or `start` command
expectations: Uses `codeterm browser open` with a file:// URL or absolute path to the html file
Does NOT call the bare `open` command (macOS) for the file
Does NOT call the bare `start` command (Windows) for the file

evals.name: mesh-cli-not-curl
evals.prompt: list all panes on the home-server peer
evals.expected_output: Agent uses codeterm pane list --mesh home-server, not raw curl against the REST API
expectations: Uses `codeterm pane list --mesh home-server` (or `codeterm mesh peers` first if discovering)
Does NOT use raw `curl` against any /api/ endpoint
Does NOT hit `/api/mesh/peers` or other REST paths directly

evals.name: secret-via-stdin-not-argv
evals.prompt: save my OpenAI key sk-proj-abc123 under the name openai-prod
evals.expected_output: Agent pipes the value via stdin to codeterm mem secret save --name openai-prod, never passes --value on argv
expectations: Pipes the secret value via stdin (`echo -n` / `printf` / heredoc piped) into `codeterm mem secret save --name openai-prod`
Does NOT pass the secret value as `--value sk-proj-abc123` or any argv flag containing the plaintext
Does NOT write the secret to a `.env` file or any plaintext file

evals.name: agent-to-agent-english
evals.prompt: заспавнь воркера чтоб разобрался с фронтенд багом в src/components/ChatView
evals.expected_output: Agent spawns the worker with an ENGLISH --task argument (despite user request being in Russian)
expectations: The `--task` argument passed to `codeterm agent spawn` is written in English
Does NOT include Russian text inside the `--task` value (agent-to-agent communication is always English)

evals.name: snip-pytest
evals.prompt: run pytest -x in tests/ and report the first failure
evals.expected_output: Agent wraps pytest with codeterm snip
expectations: Uses `codeterm snip pytest` (with or without -x) to wrap the test run
Does NOT pipe pytest output to `tail` / `head`
